title: PSLV-C62 failure and the road to Gaganyaan
text:
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) began 2026 with a setback. On 12 January 2026, its Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle mission PSLV-C62 lifted off from Sriharikota carrying EOS-N1, a strategic hyperspectral Earth-observation satellite also referred to as Anvesha, along with 15 co-passenger payloads belonging to Indian and foreign organisations. The first two stages performed as planned, but ISRO reported an anomaly at the end of the third stage, known as PS3. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said a disturbance in the rocket's roll rate had pushed the vehicle off its flight path, and the payloads did not reach their intended orbit. Among the lost payloads were Theos-2, an Earth-observation satellite built jointly by the United Kingdom and Thailand, and AyulSat, a refuelling demonstrator. The Spanish prototype Kestrel Initial Demonstrator was reported to have transmitted some data.

The failure drew attention because it was the second consecutive loss for the workhorse rocket. The previous mission, PSLV-C61 in May 2025, had also failed owing to a problem in the third stage. Reports said that a redesigned third-stage motor had undergone two static tests in October and November 2025 before C62 was cleared to fly, although the earlier committee's findings had not been made public. After C62, ISRO announced a failure analysis committee. Separately, in a departure from the agency's usual reliance on internal reviews, news reports citing sources said the government had set up a probe headed by K. VijayRaghavan, a former Principal Scientific Advisor to the Prime Minister, with former ISRO chairman S. Somanath as co-chairman. A report from Chennai dated 19 February carried the same details, but the government has not formally released the committee's findings.

The episode has implications for India's human spaceflight plans. The Gaganyaan programme, which aims to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit, depends on a series of uncrewed test flights. In January 2026 Narayanan said the first of these, G1, which will carry the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra, was about 90 per cent complete after more than 8,000 ground tests and could fly by March 2026. That date passed without a launch. The mission is now listed for the fourth quarter of 2026, on a human-rated launch vehicle, with the crewed flight pencilled in for 2027 or later. ISRO has said that three uncrewed missions will precede it.

Meanwhile, India is also building new launch infrastructure. A second spaceport, intended mainly for small satellite launches, has been under construction since March 2025, and the government has targeted commissioning in the financial year 2026-27. Officials stress, however, that the existing launch complex will remain the primary site for all major rockets, including the PSLV and the GSLV.

questions.q: The Sriharikota spaceport, from which PSLV-C62 was launched, is officially named after which scientist and former ISRO chairman?
questions.explanation: Sriharikota (earlier SHAR) hosts the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, renamed in 2002 in memory of Prof. Satish Dhawan, former ISRO chairman.

questions.assertion: India's planned second spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam in Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu, is intended mainly for launching small satellites on the SSLV.
questions.reason: A launch site on the southern tip of the peninsula lets rockets fly directly south to polar orbits, avoiding the curved trajectory that Sriharikota launches need to stay clear of Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: Kulasekarapattinam is planned for SSLV launches to Sun-synchronous polar orbits; its southern location allows a straight southward path, whereas launches from Sriharikota have to curve to avoid Sri Lanka.

list1: II. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (lead centre for launch vehicles)
questions.explanation: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru; VSSC is in Thiruvananthapuram; Sriharikota island lies in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh; Kulasekarapattinam is in Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu.

statements: I. The PSLV is a four-stage vehicle whose third stage (PS3) uses solid propellant.
II. The very first PSLV flight, PSLV-D1 on 20 September 1993, successfully placed its satellite in orbit.
questions.explanation: PSLV alternates solid-liquid-solid-liquid, so PS3 is solid (HTPB). PSLV-D1 in 1993 failed because of an attitude-control problem; the first successful flight was PSLV-D2 in October 1994.

statements: I. ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, succeeding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) set up in 1962.
II. ISRO's headquarters is located in Thiruvananthapuram.
III. ISRO functions under the Department of Space.
questions.explanation: ISRO succeeded INCOSPAR on 15 August 1969 and is managed by the Department of Space; its headquarters is in Bengaluru, not Thiruvananthapuram (where VSSC is).

questions.q: The uncrewed Gaganyaan test flight G1 is planned on a human-rated version of which ISRO launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: Gaganyaan uses HLVM3, the human-rated variant of the LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III), launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
